sessions.title: Breakfast
Welcome
sessions.description: Welcome to the 4th Annual National Rural STEM Summit from the Director of the Conference! Let's start off with some housekeeping information, and set the stage for an exciting two days of sharing and learning from people committed to improving STEM opportunities, access, and experiences across rural America!

sessions.title: Opening Remarks
sessions.description: Dr. Yir Glora Yueh is the Provost of Midwestern University. Join us as she welcomes the event, and then kicks off the MWU Tours.

sessions.title: Healthcare 2030 - A Multisector Discussion on Needs, Assets, and Pathways Across the Healthcare Spectrum
sessions.description: A panel presentation on the future of Healthcare and the Healthcare pathways over the next five to ten years. Voices from Academia, Hospital Admistration, Healthcare providers, and Workforce specialists.

sessions.title: AI in Education - Engineering Prompts for maximizing productivity
sessions.description: Discover how effective prompt engineering can transform teaching, learning, and program development. Led by Nan Williams, this interactive session equips teachers, students, and non-formal educators with practical strategies for crafting AI prompts that improve lesson planning, assessment, research, communication, and creative problem-solving. Participants will practice prompt design, compare results across AI tools, and leave with reusable templates, productivity tips, and ethical guidelines for integrating AI into classrooms and informal learning environments.

sessions.title: Connecting Educators with Environmental Professionals & Resources for meaningful STEM learning
sessions.description: Discover a network of environmental educators, natural resource professionals, and shared resources that support K–12 schools through meaningful partnerships and place-based learning. This session highlights Project Learning Tree and Fire Ecology Learning Lab resources, which make complex forest and environmental topics accessible through age-appropriate, classroom-ready lessons. Participants will explore how environmental education strengthens STEM learning by fostering critical thinking, informed decision-making, and an appreciation for diverse perspectives on environmental issues.

sessions.title: Organized Chaos: Using Evidence, Conversation, and Student Ownership to Drive STEM Learning
sessions.description: What happens when students pursue different ideas, products, and solutions while still meeting the same standards? This session explores an “organized chaos” approach to STEM learning that blends student ownership, proficiency scales, standards-based assessment, and strategic questioning to create highly engaging experiences. Through examples in engineering, coding, research, and makerspace innovation, participants will see how diverse student work can be assessed fairly using shared evidence of understanding. Attendees will leave with practical tools to increase ownership while maintaining clear expectations and accountability.

sessions.title: Understanding Learning and Workforce Systems
sessions.description: This session will give participants a shared understanding of learning and workforce systems and their attributes. It will explore important features, levers, and change agents across PK-12, Postsecondary, and Workforce systems, leaving participants with a holistic frame of reference for thinking about their local STEMM talent ecosystem. Participants can use this frame to understand the cross-system dynamics at play at a national level, and will reflect on implications in their communities, such as: 1. Identifying fragmentation points between education, workforce, and postsecondary in their own region. 2. Committing to one concrete next step for applying the shared vocabulary and levers in an upcoming meeting, project, or planning effort.

sessions.title: Break with Exhibitors
Semiconductor Partnership Programming
sessions.description: Arizona Science Center in partnership with SEMI Foundation worked with local semiconductor companies to co-create an exhibition, lead teacher PD, and plan student programming. Get a glimpse into the co-creation process and learnings on how Arizona Science Center took the onsite exhibition and turn it into an outreach program for rural communities.

sessions.title: Engaging Educators through Self-Driven Professional Learning as part of the Arizona STEM Acceleration Project (ASAP)
sessions.description: The Arizona STEM Acceleration Project is a source for teacher connection to other teachers, materials, and K-12 STEM lesson plans! But, it is centered around the idea of engaging educators through self-driven professional learning. This non-proscriptive/teacher-driven program encourages participants to think about the system they are trying to impact and engage in high quality professional development to meet their needs and the needs of their community. In this session you can engage with us in a systems thinking activity to help understand your STEM education ecosystem (whether that's in a classroom, school, district or the state) and brainstorm how increase your impact on student's learning.

sessions.title: Language Culture and STEM - Indigenous Community Co-Design for STEM Exhibit
sessions.description: Explore a community engagement process that has been used for Native Language and Cultural Preservation Programs. The process is now being piloted for use in other Indigenous Communty Engagements. This breakout will provide a sample of a multi-day workshop.

sessions.title: Place-Based Learning Connecting Field Research and Work Skills
sessions.description: With a philanthropic gift, Northern Arizona University acquired the historic Hat Ranch near Williams in 2021, creating a site for research, teaching, and outreach 70 miles south of the Grand Canyon. Faculty, staff, and students developed a summer field course connecting learners to research and workforce skills through the Colorado Plateau. This session shares lessons from implementation and highlights strategies for partnering with educators and communities. It also explores how this place-based learning model can be adapted to other rural communities to strengthen engagement and collective impact.

sessions.title: Turning Knowledge Into Action
sessions.description: Building on Session 1, this session will deepen the exploration of systems’ attributes, with a focus on getting local and specific. Participants will explore a lever or occupational priority that matters in their community and consider how they could leverage end-to-end systems insights to strengthen their approaches and impact. Participants can use time in this session to: 1. Map existing programs, initiatives, or partnerships in their community across the end-to-end frame of reference introduced in the session. 2. Explore how NAICS, SOC, and CIP codes can be used together as neutral building blocks for mapping STEMM learning to career pathways. 3. Prioritize two to three regional “levers” that could strengthen crosssector STEMM conversations.

sessions.title: Lunch with Table Talk
Smithsonian STARS- Scientists Taking Astronomy to Rural Schools
sessions.description: The Smithsonian STARS program connects classrooms to the cosmos through a new nationwide educational initiative led by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory. STARS is designed to bring high-quality, hands-on astronomy experiences to rural schools across the United States—an investment in STEM education and the future of rural learners. The STARS vision is to spark curiosity and inspire the next generation of explorers and scientists by combining local access to dark skies with the Smithsonian’s scientific expertise. Participating schools will receive a Celestron telescope, standards-aligned astronomy lessons, teacher professional development, and a direct connection to Smithsonian science. This talk will highlight the mission of the STARS program and how rural schools can get involved. It will also provide hands-on example activities of lessons that will be included in the program.

sessions.title: Maximum Profit, Minimum Impact: Sustainable Mining Engineering
sessions.description: In this activity, participants analyze drilled core samples to model a hypothetical ore body beneath Earth’s surface. They then design a mine that maximizes copper extraction while minimizing environmental impact. The lesson explores relationships between area, volume, density, mass, and concentration to evaluate the value of unseen mineral resources and compare it to extraction costs. Participants will consider real-world mining decision-making factors. The activity can be scaled for grades 6–12, from basic algebra through calculus.

sessions.title: AI Productivity for K-12 Educators: Tips and Tricks with Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini
sessions.description: Generative AI tools are rapidly becoming powerful assistants that can enhance the efficiency and creativity of K–12 educators. This hands-on workshop moves beyond fear and hype to focus on practical, ethical, and effective strategies for integrating large language models such as Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini into daily professional workflows. Participants will explore real-world applications that streamline planning, support instruction, and expand creative possibilities while maintaining responsible and thoughtful use of AI in education.

sessions.title: "Make, Take, Collaborate” Bringing STEM to life through library partnerships
sessions.description: This presentation explores “Make and Take” STEM kits as a hands-on strategy to spark curiosity, creativity, and real-world problem-solving in both classroom and informal learning spaces. Participants will see how these kits support collaboration and applied STEM learning while increasing accessibility for diverse learners. The session also highlights partnerships with local libraries to expand resources, expertise, and community outreach. Together, educators and libraries can extend meaningful STEM experiences beyond traditional settings and strengthen community engagement.

sessions.title: Growing STEM Where You Are: Ecosystem Strategies for Rural Communities
sessions.description: You're already a Field Catalyst. You just need the system to match your energy. In this hands-on workshop, rural STEM providers and educators will discover how to stop operating in isolation and start building the connected, community-wide ecosystem your students deserve. We will explore what a STEM learning ecosystem actually looks like in a rural context, dig into national data trends hitting rural communities right now, and uncover practical strategies you can start using Monday morning. You do not need a big city budget. You need the right connections, a shared vision, and a community that is ready to grow together. We will help you map what you already have, identify the gaps, and take your first real steps toward building something bigger than any one program can do alone. Rural is not a limitation. It is your greatest asset.

sessions.title: Break with Exhibitors
From AI-Curious to AI-Capable: A Teacher’s First 30 Days with Classroom AI
sessions.description: You don’t need a PhD or expensive software to use AI effectively in the classroom. This 20-minute Flash Talk gives rural educators a practical 30-day plan to build five essential AI skills, including differentiating lessons, creating standards-aligned assessments, drafting culturally responsive communications, and developing discussion prompts. Participants will also learn when AI is not the right tool and leave with a phone-friendly resource, printable checklist, and access to a web-based AI workshop.

sessions.title: From Curiosity to Community: Bringing Authentic Research to Any Classroom
sessions.description: What does authentic research look like in a rural classroom with limited resources? This flash talk highlights how Arizona educators are engaging students in meaningful, real-world investigations using local resources and support from Arizona Science Center outreach programs. Participants will explore practical strategies for launching classroom research, supporting individual projects, and building toward science fairs. The session shares lessons from diverse school settings and demonstrates how authentic research fosters critical thinking, problem-solving, scientific communication, and long-term student engagement.

sessions.title: Using Deep Discussion in the STEM Classroom
sessions.description: This session introduces educators to practical strategies for facilitating meaningful discussion in STEM classrooms. Participants explore the foundations of “accountable talk,” where students build on one another’s ideas using evidence, active listening, and respectful communication. Through collaborative protocols such as story harvesting, Socratic seminars, and structured discussion roles, attendees experience how to create inclusive environments that amplify all student voices. The session also highlights tools like sentence stems, partner discussions, and reflective practices to support thoughtful participation. Educators examine ways to assess and evaluate discussion through rubrics, self-reflection, and participation metrics. Anchored in real-world applications like Project Arizona Wildlife, the session emphasizes connecting classroom dialogue to authentic environmental issues. By the end, participants leave with adaptable strategies, increased confidence in leading discussions, and actionable ideas to foster deeper engagement and critical thinking in their own classrooms.

sessions.title: Low-Cost, High-Impact Engineering Activities
sessions.description: Great STEM learning doesn’t require a big budget. This interactive, hands-on session explores low-cost STEM activities that spark curiosity, creativity, and collaboration using common classroom materials. Participants will engage in engineering challenges that emphasize the design process—building, testing, and improving solutions to real-world problems. The session models ways to adapt activities for different grade levels and learning environments while aligning with NGSS and academic standards. Attendees will leave with ready-to-use ideas, simple materials lists, and practical strategies for bringing hands-on STEM learning into any classroom.

sessions.title: Every Kid, Data Ready
sessions.description: This interactive mini talk demonstrates how students can build data literacy through hands-on, real-world investigations. Participants will experience a model lesson where students collect, analyze, and interpret data to explore community questions. The session highlights student-driven inquiry, collaboration, and data storytelling while showing how place-based learning increases engagement, critical thinking, and accessibility—especially in rural settings. Attendees will leave with practical strategies, ready-to-use resources, and ideas for fostering confident, data-literate learners.

sessions.title: Youth Leaders In Action: The Chief Science Officer Program
sessions.description: Learn how the Chief Science Officers program can be leveraged in your community to build youth leadership skills and support workforce development. Chief Science Officers are students in grades 6-12 who are passionate about STEM education and student voice. They act as STEM ambassadors while building their networks, preparing for their future career, and improving their confidence as leaders. CSO is a program of the SciTech Institute. Through this session, you'll get a taste of the program experience while learning how to start a CSO cohort in your school, district, or town.

sessions.title: Impacting Women in STEM: Creating Feedback Loops of Opportunity
sessions.description: Curiosity is the foundation of every STEM career, but sustaining it requires helping students feel they belong. This session explores strategies for engaging girls in STEM by using everyday systems and technologies as accessible entry points for discovery. Participants will learn how educators can foster curiosity through relatable, hands-on exploration while creating welcoming environments, providing meaningful mentorship, and connecting students to resources that build confidence and inspire long-term interest in STEM pathways.

sessions.title: Designing Rural STEM Innovation: Lessons from a Rural Aerospace Laboratory School
sessions.description: Rural communities often face barriers to equitable STEM access, including isolation, limited coursework, and fewer career-connected opportunities. This interactive showcase shares lessons from the first year of a rural aerospace-focused laboratory school developed through K–12, higher education, and industry partnerships. Participants will explore strategies for embedding hands-on STEM learning into the school day, increasing engagement and career awareness. Through discussion and design activity, attendees will identify local assets, examine partnership models, and develop adaptable STEM approaches for rural communities.

sessions.title: Bits, Bots & Building AI Literacy: AI for Tiny Techs
sessions.description: This session introduces artificial intelligence in a child-friendly way, helping young learners understand how machines can “learn” and “think.” It explores opportunities AI offers as creative tools and problem-solving partners, while emphasizing important guardrails and digital citizenship. Participants will examine how media literacy helps children distinguish between real and AI-generated information and navigate digital content responsibly. Educators will gain practical strategies for classroom discussions and age-appropriate AI exploration activities and guided learning supports for teachers.

sessions.title: Science News Learning: Boosting STEM Literacy with Science Journalism
sessions.description: Intrigued about incorporating current examples in research and the latest applications in STEM into your science activities to increase STEM literacy? Come to this session to discuss science literacy and it's importance, and explore current journalism resources that can be used to enhance STEM learning and literacy through the Science News Learning program. Discover the large libraries of Science News Media Group journalism and lesson plans that connect these real-world issues to core curricula.

sessions.title: Building the Rural STEM Ecosystem through Connection, Collaboration, and Relationships
sessions.description: Discover how to launch, strengthen, and sustain high-quality STEM education through a collaborative, community-driven model. For more than five years, the STEM Leadership Cadre has partnered with K–12 schools, higher education, and community organizations to build thriving STEM ecosystems, especially in rural and underserved communities. Participants will explore a network of STEM partners across Arizona and beyond, learn to leverage higher education, industry, and research resources, and engage in hands-on capacity-building activities. Attendees will leave with practical strategies, new connections, and actionable ideas to expand and sustain STEM opportunities for student success.

sessions.title: Engineering and Technical Institute - A Career Exploration of Willcox and Cochise County in SE Arizona
sessions.description: This session shares practices on the design of the ETI Camp that Willcox Theater and Arts hosts each year in June. Students have experiences ranging from hands-on building to field trips to a variety of STEM career sites.

sessions.title: Global Lessons for Rural AI Education: Insights from a Fulbright Specialist Experience in Senegal
sessions.description: This session shares global lessons on how artificial intelligence (AI) can support more accessible STEM education in rural contexts. Drawing on a Fulbright Specialist experience in Senegal, the presentation explores how institutions operating in resource-constrained environments can leverage AI to expand learning opportunities, strengthen teaching capacity, and address gaps in STEM access. It will examine parallels between rural communities in the United States and global contexts, where challenges such as limited resources, educator shortages, and uneven access to advanced STEM content require innovative approaches. Participants will explore how AI tools can be applied in low-resource settings to support learning and teaching, and student engagement in STEM fields. It will also equip participants with actionable insights for integrating AI into rural STEM education in ways that are scalable, ethical, and locally relevant. The discussion will highlight examples of implementation strategies, including AI-supported instruction, learning assistance tools, and professional development models for educators.

sessions.title: Co-Designing Resaerch. Community Identified Risk and Resilience: Rural Disaster Preparedness
sessions.description: This session explores disaster preparedness and recovery in rural Arizona, highlighting how geographic isolation, limited infrastructure, and scarce resources shape community resilience. Participants will learn about Co-ID, a community-led, phenomenological research approach that values residents as experts in their own communities. Through images and examples from focus group workshops, the session demonstrates how collaborative knowledge exchange informs the co-design of practical disaster preparedness resources that reflect local priorities and strengthen confidence in responding to natural disasters.

sessions.title: Cultivating Collective Impact: School Gardens as Catalysts for Community Stewardship
sessions.description: Research consistently demonstrates that garden-based learning increases student engagement, strengthens STEM understanding, and connects learning to real-world challenges. In this interactive session, participants will experience a classroom-ready garden-based STEM lesson, explore the research behind its effectiveness, and examine how community partnerships can enhance and sustain these learning opportunities. Attendees will collaborate on a hands-on investigation, discuss strategies for implementation across grade levels, and learn how schools can engage community partners to create meaningful, place-based learning experiences. Participants will leave with practical resources, an annual engagement calendar, and actionable next steps for bringing garden-based STEM learning to their students.

sessions.title: Magnifying Partnerships for Capacity Building
sessions.description: Rural communities offer powerful assets for STEM education, including place-based knowledge, strong networks, and students motivated by real-world problem solving. This session highlights SARSEF programs available to Arizona educators and students and how they have evolved in response to local needs. Participants will explore how place-based, inquiry-led approaches foster authentic belonging in STEM and engage in a hands-on research proposal activity. The session also includes reflection time to apply insights to participants’ own schools and learning communities.

sessions.title: Strengthening Sustainability Through Educator Collaboration: A Working Model Connecting Teachers & Watershed Experts
sessions.description: Come learn about the Rural Watershed STEM Fellowship, which serves communities throughout Arizona’s central Verde River Valley. Pilot-funded by the Society for Science, the fellowship explores ways to engage and empower rural educators in STEM. A unique feature of this year-long program is its collaboration with Friends of the Verde River (FVR), an environmental nonprofit whose mission is to preserve the river and support the communities that depend on it. The fellowship is the first program to bring together FVR’s subject-matter experts and educators from across the region and has the potential to serve as a model for other groups to recreate. This presentation will highlight the practices developed through the fellowship, examine its strengths and barriers, share research-informed lessons, and explore the sustained impact of this place-based professional learning experience.

sessions.title: Teen Science Cafe
sessions.description: This interactive session introduces the Teen Science Café (TSC) model and explores how it expands STEM access and career exposure for rural youth. Participants will learn how TSC connects teens with STEM professionals through youth-led events that build leadership, communication, and career readiness skills. The session highlights benefits of joining a national network of educators and professionals, including training and ongoing support. Presenters will share strategies for adapting the model for rural communities, and the session concludes with a hands-on marine science activity simulating a Teen Science Café experience.

sessions.title: Real World Applications of End-to-End Systems Thinking
sessions.description: Join this session to explore examples of how end-to-end systems thinking is being applied in real communities. Featuring examples from SciTech Institute and TIES, this session will leave participants inspired to turn understanding into action in their communities. Participants will reflect on: 1. A personal or organizational story demonstrating how a specific lever enabled or limited pathway implementation. 2. Levers to prioritize for activation in the next 6–12 months and articulate one concrete action step for each.

sessions.title: Dyad, Survey, Closing Remarks and Raffle
sessions.description: Join us for this facilitated networking experience, share your experience and insights, and let's wrap up an exciting day of learning and connecting with the chance to win prizes!

sessions.title: Summit Reception
sessions.description: Everyone is welcome to join in for an evening of light snacks, drinks, and networking opportunities, as well as conversation with Midwestern University students as they showcase their specialties.

sessions.title: Breakfast
Housekeeping/Welcome
sessions.description: Join the Conference Director for to start off the second day of the Learning Summit.

sessions.title: STEMM Leaders as Talent Builders: Using education expertise to transform career pathway and talent systems
sessions.description: Dr. Stephanie Rodriguez’s keynote positions STEMM (STEM + Medicine) learning and engagement leaders as required contributors to the talent system, and their expertise from sparking curiosity to ensuring access to foundational and authentic STEM learning as essential. She argues that STEMM leaders must understand workforce development because their programs directly influence who will be interested in, prepared for, and enter in-demand and high-quality STEMM jobs. She’ll challenge educators, ecosystem leads, community colleges and universities to “flex their education system muscles” and use familiar strengths and levers—curriculum, data, research-based pedagogy, policy, partnerships—to bridge systems and cobuild seamless pathways into STEMM opportunities in collaboration with the workforce system. On behalf of the STEMM Opportunity Alliance, she issues a broader call to action: move from isolated learning and workforce efforts to coordinated, crosssystem strategies that can smooth pathways into good STEMM careers, making opportunity more transparent and accessible for all.

sessions.title: Break with Exhibitors
Innovative Anatomy: Animal Skulls and Evolutionary Biology in the Classroom
sessions.description: Join Dr. Smith to explore engaging and cutting-edge ideas for teaching anatomy in the classroom. Using real animal skulls, 3D-printed models, and simple printouts, she will share adaptable and fun classroom activities for teaching homology and comparative anatomy, including imagined skulls designed to represent fan-favorite fictional movie animals beloved by teenagers. Dr. Smith will also discuss the exciting work being done at Midwestern’s ARCIVES project to catalog anatomical specimens, as well as online national resources teachers can access for anatomy education and peer-reviewed research.

sessions.title: Quick and Dirty Grant Writing
sessions.description: Writing grants can be daunting, at first. But like most techniques, a few tips go a long way to easing the process. This quick workshop-like presentation will start you on your grant writing journey.

sessions.title: Curious Minds: Three “What If?” Science Sandboxes Your Students Can Run on Any Chromebook
sessions.description: STEM classrooms want inquiry-based learning, but the tools that enable it — chemistry simulators, ecosystem models, planetary-science software — usually require hardware, licenses, or IT approvals that rural districts cannot reliably get. Curious Minds is three free, browser-based “what if?” sandboxes that run on any Chromebook with no install. Mix elements and watch reactions unfold. Drop a wolf into Yellowstone with no elk and trace the cascade. Build a planet at 0.3 AU around an M-dwarf star and discover whether life could exist on it. Each sandbox combines a curated scientific knowledge base with AI reasoning, returning explanations a 7th grader can follow and a STEM teacher would trust. In this 55-minute hands-on showcase, we’ll review the platform, demo each sandbox, then turn the room over to free experimentation. You’ll leave with a working tool — and the GitHub code repository to make it your own. **Bring your own laptop to play in the sandbox!

sessions.title: Connecting STEM to Local Trades
sessions.description: This STEM presentation explores practical ways to connect STEM learning to local trades in rural communities, including farming, construction, automotive repair, welding, and electrical work. Participants will learn strategies for making lessons more relevant by linking instruction to real-world applications students see in their communities. The session shares low-prep, hands-on ideas that reflect authentic job tasks and problem solving, along with approaches for engaging local professionals through guest speakers, job shadowing, and project-based learning. Attendees will leave with ready-to-use strategies that increase engagement and highlight STEM career pathways.

sessions.title: Lunch with Table Talk
When "Group Think" is Good Thinking
sessions.description: Participants will explore a science phenomenon through the lens of a student (grades 3–12) as a starting point for developing a Driving Question Board (DQB). After building the DQB, they will reflect on how it supports student sensemaking and how it can be revisited and expanded throughout a unit. The session emphasizes practical classroom application across grade levels and contexts. Participants will leave with ideas, strategies, and resources for implementing Driving Question Boards in a variety of formats.

sessions.title: Worlds of Work in Action: Designing Career Exploration that Sticks
sessions.description: Explore how immersive career exploration events like Pinal County’s Worlds of Work can transform student awareness and engagement. This session will unpack the design, partnerships, and logistics behind successful large-scale events that connect students directly with industry. Participants will gain replicable strategies for bringing hands-on, career-connected learning to their own communities.

sessions.title: You Don’t Know If You Don’t Try! Building Rural STEM Opportunities Through Grants and Partnerships
sessions.description: Rural educators often have innovative ideas but limited funding, time, or support to bring them to life. This session shares how a school turned ideas into STEM opportunities through grants, partnerships, advocacy programs, and AI tools. Participants will explore strategies for finding funding, building collaborations, and using AI to support brainstorming, proposals, communication, and planning. Examples from organizations such as Society for Science, Toshiba America Foundation, and Rural Schools Collaborative illustrate scalable success. Attendees will leave with resources, AI prompts, and practical steps to confidently pursue STEM opportunities in rural schools.

sessions.title: All for STEAM! Strategies and activities for creating creating neurodiversity-affirming
sessions.description: Explore inclusive strategies and hands-on activities specifically designed to support neurodiverse learners within dynamic STEAM classrooms. Grounded in findings from a multi-year National Science Foundation (NSF) research project, this session delves into the practical application of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles. We ensure that science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics are accessible to students with varying cognitive profiles, such as autism, ADHD, and dyslexia. Participants will learn how to move beyond a "one-size-fits-all" approach by providing varied entry points that allow students to engage with complex concepts through their preferred modalities. We will examine how to create a truly flexible learning environment, incorporating sensory-friendly tools and adaptive technologies, that meets the diverse needs of every student. Every attendee will leave with a comprehensive guidebook of best practices and a toolkit of actionable techniques to lower barriers to participation and inspire confidence in all budding innovators

sessions.title: Break with Exhibitors
Globe at Night and STEM Resources with NOIR Labs
sessions.description: NSF’s NOIRLab Globe at Night program is an international citizen-science campaign that engages people in measuring night sky brightness to raise awareness of light pollution and its impacts on energy use, wildlife, and health. This session explores how youth and families can become citizen scientists, analyze data, and connect light pollution to environmental issues, while providing educators with free resources and a PBL opportunity to design community-based solutions. Participants will also explore NOIRLab's education outreach programs and get a view into the new Science Museum.

sessions.title: Creating Life-long Learners and Successful Healthcare Providers: A Model for Teaching Critical Thinking
sessions.description: Our country faces a growing shortage of physicians and other healthcare providers, particularly in rural areas. While research shows that medical school applicants from rural areas are more likely to practice rural medicine upon graduation, in the last decade, only 36-41% of overall applicants were admitted to medical school, and many applicants from rural backgrounds did not have competitive ‘traditional’ application metrics (GPA and MCAT scores). Our research indicates that otherwise unsuccessful applicants can be trained in a graduate-level program, accepted into medical school, and become successful practicing physicians. Major findings from our research include: Traditional admissions metrics poorly predicts medical school performance Graduate Biomedical Sciences program GPA strongly predicts medical school rank and licensing board outcomes Compared to non-Biomed peers, Biomed alumni show greater leadership, research participation, critical thinking, and diversity During this workshop, we will discuss some of the reasons why we think the MWU Biomedical Sciences program is successful for non-traditional students, demonstrate hands-on classroom activities, and share ideas for inspiring and launching rural students into healthcare careers.

sessions.title: Growing Our Own: How AZTRAP Builds Rural Educator Pipelines
sessions.description: Rural communities face persistent challenges in recruiting and retaining qualified educators. Arizona’s Registered Teacher Apprenticeship Program (AZTRAP) offers a scalable “grow-your-own” model that aligns workforce development with teacher preparation. This session explores how a federally registered apprenticeship supports aspiring educators in rural and high-need areas through paid, mentored, classroom-based training paired with an educator preparation program. Participants will learn how agencies collaborate to reduce financial barriers, strengthen local pipelines, and improve retention, while gaining design insights, early lessons learned, and practical tools for replicating apprenticeship pathways in their own communities.

sessions.title: Building Rural Computer Science Pathways: A Scalable Ecosystem for Teacher Professional Development and Classroom Integration
sessions.description: This breakout session presents a pipeline ecosystem designed to expand computer science (CS) education in rural communities. It builds teacher capacity through two pathways: a certification track supporting educators in earning CS credentials and teaching courses, and an entry-level track introducing foundational CS and computational thinking through local training. Together, they create multiple entry points for students and strengthen regional expertise. The session includes an AI-enhanced, hands-on activity using the Microsoft FarmBeats curriculum, connecting CS to agriculture and rural contexts, along with key design lessons for scalable, community-centered adoption.

sessions.title: Break
Leveraging Civil Air Patrol STEM programs to support student engagement with real world workforce
sessions.description: This breakout session introduces Civil Air Patrol K–12 STEM kits and aviation-based learning opportunities for both students and educators. Participants will explore hands-on, standards-aligned activities that connect aerospace concepts to classroom learning, including flight science, engineering design, and real-world problem solving. The session highlights pathways for student engagement through aviation careers and youth programs, while also showcasing professional learning opportunities for teachers. Attendees will leave with ready-to-use resources, implementation strategies, and ideas for integrating aviation STEM into K–12 classrooms.

sessions.title: Healthcare STEM Careers and Middle School Curriculum
sessions.description: Joseph Sepp Sprietsma and Jason Zibart will showcase the Benson Future Superhero Academy, an innovative summer program connecting rural youth ages 11–16 with healthcare careers. Through hands-on clinical and hospital leadership experiences, participants explore high-demand professions while building career pathways. Attendees will learn how this scalable partnership among healthcare, education, and workforce organizations helps rural communities develop local talent, strengthen STEM career pipelines, and support long-term community health.

sessions.title: Real Data, Real Impact: How Rural Students Can Map, Protect, and Save Arizona’s Streams
sessions.description: Did you know we don't know the flow patterns for 83% of Arizona’s streams? Guess what, your students can change that with just a smartphone or a GPS! Join us for this high-energy, hands-on breakout session where we turn community science into an outdoor adventure. You’ll get moving, test-drive user-friendly mapping apps, and get up close with actual scientific equipment. We will show you exactly how easy it is to bring a real-world community science project back to your school. By the end of this session, you’ll be fully equipped to transform your local waterways into a living laboratory. Come ready to move, play, and discover how your rural classroom can provide the critical data needed to protect Arizona’s streams. Let’s map the flow together!

sessions.title: FarmBeats For MiddleSchool
sessions.description: Teachers will compare soil types and investigate water-holding capacity through hands-on activities. Using a micro:bit kit, participants will build a simple soil moisture sensor and program it with Microsoft MakeCode to collect and analyze data from different samples. The session explores adaptations for middle school classrooms, including inquiry-based learning, engineering design, and data analysis. It concludes with a discussion of how precision agriculture technologies support sustainability and broader applications in environmental science and STEM education.

sessions.title: Survey, Closing Remarks and Raffle
sessions.description: Join us as we wrap up this year's experience. Share your insights on what worked, what didn't, and how we can continue growing and expanding opportunities. Bring your ticket for a chance to win prizes!

presenters.name: Alison Smith
presenters.bio: Alyson Smith is the Senior Vice President of Engagement at Arizona Science Center. In this role she leads educational innovation and hands on engagement opportunities through management of the science center’s Learning teams. Alyson previously served in several learning and engagement roles at Arizona Science Center including as a STEM instructor, the Director of Youth Programs, and as Vice President of Informal Learning. Alyson started her career as an elementary school teacher through Teach for America. Alyson received a BA in Psychology and Sociology from Emory University and a Master's in Elementary Education from Arizona State University. She is proud to be an advocate for STEM education across the state of Arizona.

presenters.name: Amanda Whitehurst
presenters.bio: Amanda Whitehurst is a former elementary and middle school teacher with a Masters of Engineering in STEM for Middle School from ASU. She is the co-founder of STEMteachersPHX, an AAPT/AIP Master Teacher Policy Fellow, Co-Founder of the Arizona Cactus Caucus, co-creator of the "Get Set for STEM" scholarship program, Certified Modeling Instructor, and Waters Center Advanced Facilitator. She is currently the Co-PI and Senior Program Manager for the Arizona STEM Acceleration Project; founded with a $10M grant from the Arizona Department of Education, and currently supported by the APS Foundation, which in its first 3 years supported over 1000 STEM teacher fellowships across Arizona and impacted almost 180K students.

presenters.name: Anna Pawlow
presenters.bio: Anna Pawlow is a STEM education leader with nearly two decades of experience designing curriculum, building educator communities, and leading national programs that expand access to high-quality science research and learning. As Director of STEM Education Outreach at Society for Science, she oversees a portfolio of national and regional outreach programs that support educators, students, and communities nationwide. These programs help educators create and expand authentic student research opportunities while using STEM journalism to strengthen science literacy and connect students to real-world discovery. Previously, Anna served as Director of STEM Literacy and Curriculum, leading Science News Learning. Before joining Society for Science, she spent 10 years as a high school science teacher in Washington, DC, where she developed inquiry-based curriculum and supported students through teaching, advising, mentoring, and leadership programs. Anna holds a Master of Chemical and Life Sciences from the University of Maryland and a Bachelor of Science in Chemistry from the College of William & Mary.

presenters.name: Anna Proctor
presenters.bio: Anna Proctor is a Post-Doctoral Researcher at ULRI's Institute for Research Experiences and Education. Her MS and PhD are in Occupational and Environmental Health from the University of Iowa. Her research focuses on rural disaster preparedness, community resilience, and safety science in rural communities.

presenters.name: Annette Koweek
presenters.bio: Annette Koweek retired in 2024 from a rural district in southeastern Arizona where she taught 6th, 7th, and 8th grade science, and was the school nurse. She is passionate about accessible K-12 science for all students and enjoys connecting with science teachers around the state as a Professional Learning Specialist for ASTA. When not learning about science herself, she enjoys hiking, fishing, and various needle arts.

presenters.name: Ashton Grove
presenters.bio: Learn how the Chief Science Officers program can be leveraged in your community to build youth leadership skills and support workforce development. Chief Science Officers are students in grades 6-12 who are passionate about STEM education and student voice. They act as STEM ambassadors while building their networks, preparing for their future career, and improving their confidence as leaders. CSO is a program of the SciTech Institute. Through this session, you'll get a taste of the program experience while learning how to start a CSO cohort in your school, district, or town.

presenters.name: Bethany Ligon
presenters.bio: Bethany Ligon is an instructional coach with Casa Grande Union High School District in Arizona and a former science teacher who is passionate about making learning engaging, meaningful, and accessible for all students. She enjoys working alongside teachers to turn big ideas into practical classroom experiences that spark curiosity, encourage collaboration, and help students think deeply about the world around them. Much of her work centers on inquiry, academic language, and creating opportunities for all learners—especially those in rural schools and communities—to see themselves as confident learners and problem-solvers. Bethany believes the best professional learning is interactive, relevant, and something educators can immediately put into practice.

presenters.name: Carleton ‘Buck’ Jones, Ph.D.
presenters.bio: Carleton ‘Buck’ Jones, Ph.D., is an Associate Professor of Biomedical Sciences at Midwestern University in Glendale, AZ. He received his doctorate in Pharmacology from Washington State University in 1999, followed by postdoctoral training at Ohio State University. He has been teaching courses in Pharmacology and Research at Midwestern since 2002. The focus of his current research is the validity of admissions criteria in predicting graduate performance and eventual success in health professional school.

presenters.name: Christelle Scharff
presenters.bio: Dr. Christelle Scharff is a Professor of Computer Science, Associate Dean, and Co-Director of the AI Lab at Pace University in New York City. She holds a Ph.D. in Symbolic Artificial Intelligence (Theorem Proving and Automated Deduction) from INRIA, the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science and Technology. Her research focuses on global software engineering, mobile technology and machine learning, and she has published more than 40 peer-reviewed papers in these areas. She has received research and educational grants from the NSF, IBM, Microsoft, VentureWell, and Google. Dr. Scharff is both a U.S. Fulbright Scholar and a U.S. Fulbright Specialist, having conducted projects in Senegal.

presenters.name: Cori Araza
presenters.bio: Dr. Cori Araza has spent over twenty years doing what she loves most — connecting higher education to K–12 to open doors for students and teachers alike. As Executive Director of K–12 Services and Solutions at Grand Canyon University, she leads the STEM Leadership Cadre, building STEM pipelines with the Engineering, Technology, and Natural Sciences colleges at GCU and beyond. She is a recognized speaker and influencer in K-12 STEM programming, bringing research-backed teaching strategies to educators at all levels. Her doctoral work focused on technology as a tool for deeper learning.

presenters.name: Cori Dennis
presenters.bio: Cori Dennis is the Coordinator of High School Outreach and Summer Programs for the University of Arizona College of Engineering. She leads K–12 STEM outreach initiatives that inspire students to explore engineering through hands-on learning, industry partnerships, and innovative summer programs. With more than 20 years of experience in education, including roles as a special education teacher, district administrator, and higher education professional, Cori is passionate about expanding access to engineering education for all students. She is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Higher Education at the University of Arizona, with research interests focused on college access, student success, and creating equitable pathways into STEM fields. Through her work, she is committed to building partnerships that strengthen Arizona's future engineering workforce and empower the next generation of innovators.

presenters.name: Dan Moreno
presenters.bio: After serving as a high school science teacher in rural WI for 16 years, Dan moved to Tucson and the University of Arizona to pursue a PhD in science teaching and teacher education. As part of his graduate studies, he connected with the School of Mining Engineering & Mineral Resources in the University's College of Engineering to design curriculum and teacher professional learning opportunities. Since then, Dan has traveled the country facilitating workshops on mineral resource and mining education for teachers, as well as classroom lessons, demonstrations, and exhibitions at school and community STEAM events, college fairs, and career days.

presenters.name: Dani Wright
presenters.bio: Dani Wright is the Chief Programs Officer for the Southern Arizona Research, Science and Engineering Foundation (SARSEF), a STEM-education nonprofit serving Arizona PreK-12 students since 1955. In her role, she develops critical thinking and problem-solving programming that serves 35,000 students and 400 educators annually, with a particular focus on expanding access in underrepresented and rural communities. Dani demonstrates a deep passion for STEM education and a steadfast commitment to creating exceptional opportunities for students to engage in authentic research. She holds a BA in Theatre Studies from Brigham Young University and is currently pursuing a graduate degree in Media, Ethics, and Social Change through the University of Sussex.

presenters.name: Dede Henderson
presenters.bio: Dede Henderson is beginning her 29th year at South Hamilton Community Schools in Jewell, Iowa, where she is a STEM/TAG instructor and science fair sponsor. Through hands-on, project-based learning, she helps students develop curiosity, confidence, and a sense of responsibility for their community and environment. Dede is a former Society for Science Advocate, a 2025 Rural Schools Collaborative Grants in Place Fellow, and a recipient of the Presidential Innovation Award for Environmental Educators.

presenters.name: Desiree Clark
presenters.bio: Desiree Clark is a dedicated middle school educator with 18 years of teaching experience. She is passionate about creating engaging, hands-on learning experiences that inspire curiosity and critical thinking. By integrating technology, STEM activities, and real-world problem-solving into her classroom, she helps students develop the skills they need for future success. Her goal is to foster a supportive learning environment where every student can grow academically, build confidence, and discover a love of learning.

presenters.name: Diane Ryan
presenters.bio: I recently retired after 47 years of teaching at the high school level. My passion is working with ASTA and being able to spread the information about AZ Science Standards in my role as an ambassador for the organization. In addition, I am the regional ASTA director for Yavapai county.

presenters.name: Emma Marcucci
presenters.bio: Dr. Emma Marcucci is the Executive Director of the Smithsonian STARS program, bringing over a decade of experience in science education and a deep commitment to making STEM accessible to all learners. A planetary scientist by training with a Ph.D. in Geological Sciences, her passion for rural and community-based education was forged during her postdoctoral work in Alaska, where she delivered customized astronomy programs to local Fairbanks schools and remote Arctic villages using a traveling planetarium. Before leading STARS, she served as the Branch Manager for Science Communications and Engagement at the Space Telescope Science Institute and as Co-Investigator for NASA's Universe of Learning. Dr. Marcucci is thrilled to join you today to share how the STARS program is building sustainable partnerships to empower educators and inspire the next generation STEM leaners through hands on experiences with telescopes.

presenters.name: Grant Lapinski
presenters.bio: Grant Lapinski is an Apprenticeship Specialist and Education Program Specialist at the Arizona Department of Education, where he supports the development and implementation of the Arizona Teacher Registered Apprenticeship Program. With five years of experience in Arizona’s K–12 system and previous experience teaching English in Japan, Grant brings both local insight and global perspective to expanding high-quality educator pathways. His work focuses on building sustainable apprenticeship models that strengthen teacher preparation and workforce development statewide. Grant’s international teaching experience and extensive travel inform his commitment to cultural understanding and learner-centered practices. He holds a Master of Education and a B.A. in History from the University of Arizona.

presenters.name: Heather F. Smith, Ph.D.
presenters.bio: Heather Smith, Ph.D., is a Professor of Anatomy at Midwestern University in Glendale, AZ. She received her Master of Arts from Stony Brook University in 2003, followed by a doctorate from Arizona State University in 2008. She has been teaching courses in Anatomy at Midwestern since 2018 and currently serves as the Editor in Chief of the national peer-reviewed Anatomical Record. She is a co-founder of the Arizona Research Collection for Integrative Vertebrate Education and Study (ARCIVES), an integrative anatomical research center developed to promote understanding of vertebrate morphology and its applications to clinical medicine, conservation biology, evolutionary biology, and the diversity of vertebrate life.

presenters.name: Isac Artzi
presenters.bio: Dr. Isac Artzi is Associate Professor and Graduate Program Chair for Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Game Development in the College of Engineering and Technology at Grand Canyon University, where he has taught full-time since 2012. His cross-disciplinary background spans mathematics, computer science, instructional design, and clinical mental health counseling, with a BS from Ben Gurion University, an MS in Computer Science from Michigan State University, a PhD in Instructional Design for Online Learning from Capella University, a Data Science Specialization from Johns Hopkins, and an MS in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from GCU. Before academia he served as Chief Technology Evangelist at AppStream (acquired by Symantec) and led distance-learning systems at Gilat Communications, and he is co-inventor on three U.S. patents in predictive streaming and edge caching. His current scholarship sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence and mental healthcare; his book "Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health: A Practical Guide for Counseling in the Digital Age" is in production with Routledge (Taylor & Francis), and his published work also includes chapters in Springer Nature's Financial Data Analytics (2022), the (ISC)² InfoSecurity Professional magazine. He is the founder and CEO of SenSym, LLC, where his interdisciplinary team applies AI to the practical work across multiple disciplines.

presenters.name: Jacqueline Jordan Spiegel, M.S., PA-C, DFAAPA, CHSE
presenters.bio: For the past 20 years, Ms. Spiegel has been a Professor and Director of Clinical Skills and Simulation at Midwestern University, overseeing simulation operations for both the Glendale, Arizona, and Downers Grove, Illinois campuses, including high-fidelity mannikins, standardized patient training, mock ER and OR rooms, clinical skills training, and real-time integrated feedback. She is a board-certified Physician Associate (PA) with expertise in emergency medicine and endocrinology. Her interests include organizational leadership, community outreach, and simulation in healthcare education. She is a distinguished fellow of the American Academy of Physician Associates and the Past President of the Arizona State Association of PAs. Her background in healthcare, work in higher education, and longevity in simulated training environments provide a unique perspective on the future of healthcare education and the adaptive skills students will need to succeed, including critical thinking, emotional intelligence, and communication.

presenters.name: Jason Zibart
presenters.bio: Jason Zibart is the Rural Executive Director of Community Health for TMC Health, where he leads innovative, community-driven strategies to improve health outcomes across rural southeastern Arizona, including Benson Hospital and Northern Cochise Community Hospital. With deep expertise in rural health program development, Jason focuses on addressing social drivers of health through initiatives such as Food Is Medicine, care coordination, and workforce pipeline development. He is known for building strong cross-sector partnerships with local government, schools, farmers, and public health agencies to expand access to care and strengthen community resilience. Jason was the NOSORH’s 2020 Community Health Star, ARHA’s 2022 Exceptional Rual Health Professional, University of Arizona Cooperative Extension’s 2024 Extensionist of the Year, and a 2024 Flinn-Brown Fellow.

presenters.name: Jen Petersen
presenters.bio: Jen Petersen serves as the Fair Director for the Arizona Science and Engineering Fair (AzSEF) and is the Manager of STEM Competitions and Outreach at Arizona Science Center. She works with educators across Arizona to expand access to authentic research experiences, helping teachers and students engage in meaningful, inquiry-driven STEM learning. Jen is passionate about supporting schools in building sustainable research and science fair programs, particularly in underserved and rural communities.

presenters.name: Jenny Conklin-Frank
presenters.bio: Jenny Frank is the Director of the STEM Ecosystem Initiative at TIES Gobal, where she leads a community of practice of 120+ community-based STEM ecosystems across 43 states and 8 countries. With over 20 years in public education — as a middle and secondary science teacher, building principal, curriculum director, professional developer, and edTech leader with Harvard's LabXchange — Jenny's consulting work brings a practitioner's lens to systems-level change focused on helping communities move beyond programs in silos to building coordinated and connected learning that offers real opportunity for every learner.

presenters.name: Joseph Sepp Sprietsma
presenters.bio: Before joining the Center for the Future of Arizona, Joseph “Sepp” Sprietsma worked with the University of Arizona Cooperative Extension’s Building Healthy Communities initiative, a four-year, $3 million collective-impact partnership addressing public health, economic development, the opioid epidemic, food security, PPE distribution, and community leadership in Cochise County. His career also includes juvenile justice reform, youth and adult learning programs, and statewide training in Motivational Interviewing and Adverse Childhood Experiences, and he continues to teach and develop curriculum for the Arizona Foundation for Legal Services and Education and Cochise College Adult Education. Sepp serves in leadership and volunteer roles with the Bisbee Engineering Science Research Center, Rural Activation Innovation Network, Benson Hospital, and the Volunteer Interfaith Caregiver Program. He holds degrees from Northern Arizona University, The Evergreen State College, and Yavapai College, completed secondary teacher training at Prescott College, and is a Tecolote Fellow with St. John’s College.

presenters.name: Julie Euber
presenters.bio: Julie Euber is CEO of SARSEF. In this role, she builds and supports a strong community of staff, board members, partners, and supporters that can strategically bring SARSEF closer to its mission of creating Arizona’s next generation of critical thinkers and problem solvers through science and engineering. Previously, she served as TGen’s Manager of Education and Outreach where she increased the community’s working knowledge of genomics and educated, trained, and inspired the next generation of researchers and physicians. She holds a BA in Anthropology and English with a minor in biology from Indiana University and earned her MA in Anthropology with a focus in Bioarchaeology from Arizona State University. Julie is an alumna of City Year New York and the American Express Leadership Academy at the ASU Lodestar Center for Philanthropy and Nonprofit Innovation. She was President of the Young Nonprofit Professionals Network of Phoenix in 2020, received a Tucson 40 under 40 award in 2021, graduated from the Greater Tucson Leadership Lead Tucson program in 2022, was a Flinn-Brown Fellow with the Arizona Center for Civic Leadership at the Flinn Foundation in 2022, and was selected to be part of the Sun Devil 100 Class of 2025 and 2026. Currently, Julie serves as Board President of the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence, is a member of the Leadership Council for ASU Lodestar Center for Philanthropy and Nonprofit Innovation, and is a board member at Birdability.

presenters.name: Kal Mannis
presenters.bio: Kalman Mannis brings over two decades of expertise in STEM education, rural community engagement, and ecosystem development. Currently serving as Senior Director for Rural Engagement at the Arizona Science Center, he has led multiple initiatives bridging computer science education, NASA programs, and community partnerships across Arizona's diverse regions. As Co-I and Project Manager for Computer Science for All, the National Rural STEM Learning Summit, and Senior Contributor to NASA's Broadening Participation with STEM Ecosystems, Kalman has facilitated strategic initiatives with K-12 districts and community organizations, developed professional learning communities, and coached implementation teams. His work with the Rural Activation and Innovation Network (RAIN) has stimulated a statewide collaborative mindset focusing on STEM awareness assets and needs in rural Arizona. With a BSc in Molecular Biology and Physics from Vanderbilt University and an MEd from the University of Phoenix, Kalman's career spans classroom teaching, instructional coaching, administration, and program leadership. He has served on numerous advisory boards and been a Fellow with DoD STEM, SLECoP’s STEM NEXT, ASU/ULRI Sustainability Education, and Project CENTRL – Center for Rural Leadership. Boards include Arizona First Things First, White Mountain Nature Center, Friends of the Verde River, and Professionals and Educators Across Cochise (PEAC). Kalman's collaborative approach connects educators, researchers, and community stakeholders to create sustainable, place-based STEM learning opportunities across generations and locations.

presenters.name: Kathia Antillon
presenters.bio: Kathia Antillon is the Engineering Capstone Instructor at Grand Canyon University in the College of Engineering & Technology. In her role, she focuses on guiding engineering students through the Capstone Design pathway starting sophomore year and culminating with the year-long capstone experience their senior year. Kathia's involvement at Grand Canyon University also includes various committee positions, serving as the Advisor to the Society of Women Engineers (SWE) chapter and teaching as an adjunct professor in various colleges. She holds a BS in Chemistry and BA in Spanish Literature from the University of Arizona, as well as an MS in Medicinal Chemistry from the University of Kansas and an MS in Mental Health and Wellness from Grand Canyon University.

presenters.name: Katie Dion
presenters.bio: Driven by a lifelong love of marine biology and scuba diving, I’ve built a career creating hands-on STEM experiences that inspire curiosity and leadership in youth. As the Program Associate for the Teen Science Café Network, a program of STEM Next, I’ve helped launch 100+ programs nationwide, and developed the flagship Teen Catalyst program, mentoring 75+ teens in communication, event coordination, and professional career skills. I also have previous experience in managing a Noyce NSF grant supporting the development of culturally responsive STEM teachers, have designed hands-on curriculum spanning all ages and programs that connect students to real-world marine and environmental science, am a former Coordinator for a summer STEM camp serving over 100 children weekly ages 4-18, and a former aquarist overseeing the care of tropical marine species at the John. G. Shedd Aquarium. Overall, I’m passionate about empowering the next generation of innovators to explore, lead, and thrive in STEM.

presenters.name: Kelsie Murphy
presenters.bio: Kelsie Murphy is the Education Development Specialist for the Smithsonian STARS program, a nationwide initiative bringing astronomy education to rural schools across the United States. She holds a Bachelor's degree in Elementary and Special Education from Northern Arizona University and Master’s in Natural Science and Environmental Education from Hamline University. Before joining STARS, Kelsie worked in public education for 7 years as both an elementary school teacher and as the director for a local STEM center in Central and Northern Arizona. She is passionate about increasing access to quality STEM education to all students and contributes to this mission through her work with STARS.

presenters.name: Laurie Altringer
presenters.bio: Laurie Altringer is the founder and director of the Science Vortex of the Verde Valley. Her experiences as an educator, community program developer and grant writer have led me to pursue my dream of opening a high-quality, engaging and hands-on science, technology, engineering, art, and mathematics (STEAM) center that will provide children creative STEAM learning opportunities that positively influence their critical thinking abilities while having fun! She has a Bachelor's in Science in Elementary Education (K-8) from Northern Arizona University, a Master's in Education in Environmental Education (with field studies focused on the Colorado Plateau) from Huxley College at Western Washington University, and a certificate in Leadership and Environmental Ethics from National Outdoor Leadership School (NOLS). She has been a certified K-8 teacher for 23 years.

presenters.name: Leslie Bell
presenters.bio: Leslie Bell is the Formal Learning & Engagement Manager at the Phoenix Zoo, where she oversees a wide range of educational initiatives, including Camp, Outreach, Family, and Teacher Programs. Passionate about conservation and environmental education, she is dedicated to creating engaging learning experiences that inspire people of all ages to connect with wildlife and become stewards of the natural world. Leslie holds a master’s degree in Curriculum and Instruction and has more than 15 years of experience in education, having taught in both traditional classroom settings and informal learning environments.

presenters.name: Lisa Lewis
presenters.bio: Lisa Lewis has dedicated more than 24 years to the library profession starting her career in a small K-12 school in rural Arizona. She is currently serving as the Library Manager for the Town of Florence since August of 2022. Prior to moving to Florence, she was the library manager for the City of Show Low. A strong advocate for rural and small libraries, Lisa has served as president of both the National Association for Rural and Small Libraries and the Arizona Library Association. Her commitment to libraries and community engagement has extended internationally, including an invitation from the U.S. Embassy to deliver a series of literacy and community engagement workshops to Croatian librarians. Throughout her career, Lisa has championed the vital role libraries play in building stronger, more connected rural communities.

presenters.name: Megan Lasley
presenters.bio: Megan Lasley is the Forestry Outreach Coordinator at the Arizona Department of Forestry and Fire Management (AZ DFFM). Her work supports the Specialized Forestry Programs and agency by sharing information and engaging the public, partners, and others in DFFM programs. Megan develops informational materials, hosts and participates in events, and is the editor of the Arizona Forestry in Focus e-newsletter. She sits on multiple working groups and committees to support outreach efforts on various forestry topics, and is a facilitor of Project Learning Tree in Arizona.

presenters.name: Meghan Smart
presenters.bio: Meghan Smart is a Principal Scientist and Community Science & Education Coordinator at the Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ), a role she enthusiastically calls "the best job ever!" With two decades of experience researching and protecting Arizona’s streams, wetlands, and waterways, Meghan is a field-tested scientist turned community champion. A leader in environmental innovation, she has launched key statewide initiatives, including groundbreaking intermittent stream research, innovative environmental "LABraries," and the AZ Community Science Alliance program. She empowers community members to take direct action for Arizona's air, water, and land through credible data collection and education. Meghan holds a B.S. in Natural Resources from the University of Arizona. When she isn't driving community-led science, she’s usually behind a camera lens, exploring national parks, or unwinding with her family at their off-grid cabin.

presenters.name: Nan Williams
presenters.bio: Over the past 40 plus years, I have been a classroom teacher, EdTech coach, Director of EdTech AZDOE, Director of Technology for two districts in Phoenix, a Student Teacher Supervisor, and now fulfills the role of Executive Director for AzTEA. I currently serve on the AZSBE Professional Practices Advisory Committee and previously served on AZDOE Technology Task Force, Ed Tech Standard Revision, Arizona Content-Area Organizations Committees. I have facilitated online courses for over 10 plus years. I believe that education is the great equalizer in our country and that it is our responsibility to prepare our students for any opportunity they wish to pursue. I have earned both my ISTE Certified EdTEch Leader and CETL.

presenters.name: Nancy Parra-Quinlan
presenters.bio: Nancy Parra-Quinlan is the 2022 Arizona State Teacher of the Year, the 2022 Air& Space Forces Association/Rolls-Royce National Teacher of the Year and the 2024 Civil Air Patrol National Aerospace Teacher of the Year. She taught STEM/CTE at Kino Junior High School in the Mesa Public School District. And is the director of the Mesa School District Aerospace Academy summer program which provides 6th , 7th, and 8th grade students with experiences in flight and space. She earned her bachelor’s degree in Elementary Education- Bilingual/Multicultural and ESL, master’s degree in Elementary Education, and an honorary doctorate in Humane Letters from Northern Arizona University. She is a National Board-Certified Teacher in Career and Technical Education. After spending 32-years teaching, she is now the coordinator for the Mesa Schools’ Paws & Peers Therapy Dog program and the Elementary Enrichment Program. Her dogs, Olaf and Bear, are therapy dogs with the program. Ms. Parra-Quinlan is a major in the Civil Air Patrol. She serves as the Assistant Director of Aerospace Education for the Arizona Wing and is the Aerospace Education Officer in the Falcon Field squadron.

presenters.name: Nicole R Lasky Garcia
presenters.bio: Nicole Lasky Garcia is School & Community Programs Manager at Explora Science Center and Children’s Museum in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Her work at Explora focuses on working with educators and the community to bring hands-on inquiry based learning to classrooms across New Mexico. Her work also includes working with colleagues to develop and facilitate curriculum for programming as well as teacher professional developments workshops. Ms. Lasky Garcia holds a graduate degree in secondary education and undergraduate degree in biology.

presenters.name: Rachael White
presenters.bio: Dr. Rachel S. White is an experienced educator, researcher, and leader specializing in STEM and aerospace education. Rachel S. White is the director of the Aerospace Academy of the Eastern Shore of VA which is a Virginia College Partnership Lab School through Old Dominion University.

presenters.name: Rae Mask
presenters.bio: Rae Mask is an instructional coach turned IT Supervisor who never stopped thinking like a teacher. With 13+ years in education and a specialty in making technology feel less intimidating and more irresistible, she leads district-wide tech integration for the Balsz School District.

presenters.name: Rob Sparks
presenters.bio: Rob Sparks is in the Communications, Education and Engagement group at NSF’s NOIRLab. He earned his B.A. in Physics from Grinnell College and M.S. in Physics from Michigan State University. He has a long career in education which includes teaching at the Good Hope School on St. Croix, Saint Stepehen’s Episcopal School in Bradenton, Florida, Manatee Community College in Bradent, Florida and the Prairie School in Racine, Wisconsin. He received the Fermilab Teacher Fellowship where he spent a year working on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. He spent a summer at the National Radio Astronomy Observatory as part of the Research Experience For Teachers program. At night he is frequently onstage at Unscrewed Theater in Tucson and performing cabaret style musical revues with One Rehearsal Short. He can frequently be found running on the trails of Tucson.

presenters.name: Ryan Palmer, Ed.D., M.F.A.
presenters.bio: Ryan Palmer, Ed.D., M.F.A., is a nationally recognized leader in health sciences education with over two decades of experience in academic medicine, clinical training, and educational innovation. Dr. Palmer’s leadership career includes positions as Associate Dean of Medical Education at Northeast Ohio Medical University (NEOMED), Education Director for the Oregon Rural Scholars Program—a flagship rural physician pipeline—and faculty appointments at Oregon Health and Science University (OHSU) and NEOMED. He has also served as Chief Academic Officer and VP for Business Development at AMOpportunities, a leading clinical rotation marketplace, bringing a rare combination of academic and industry leadership to rural health workforce challenges. Rural health education is the foundation of Dr. Palmer’s scholarship. His doctoral dissertation—“Exploring Online Community Among Rural Medical Education Students”—earned him the 2014 Carnegie Project on the Education Doctorate Dissertation in Practice Award, a national honor for doctoral work that drives meaningful change in practice. Dr. Palmer is also the creator of the TeleOSCE, one of the first telemedicine simulations in U.S. medical education, designed specifically to help students understand the realities facing rural patients. Dr. Palmer’s peer-reviewed work appears in Academic Medicine, Rural and Remote Health, Family Medicine, and MedEdPORTAL, among others. He holds an Ed.D. from Portland State University, an M.F.A from DePaul University, and a B.A. Magna Cum Laude from California State University, Chico.

presenters.name: Ryan Salcido
presenters.bio: Ryan Salcido is an Apprenticeship Specialist and Education Program Specialist with the Arizona Department of Education, where he supports the expansion and implementation of the Arizona Teacher Registered Apprenticeship Program. A former band director with 12 years of experience in Arizona public schools, Ryan brings deep expertise in program design, assessment systems, and student-centered instruction. His background includes leading instrumental music programs across multiple districts, developing assessment frameworks, managing budgets, and coordinating district and state festivals—consistently earning “Superior” performance ratings. Ryan applies this instructional and operational experience to strengthen educator preparation pathways, streamline reporting systems, and support schools in adopting high-quality apprenticeship models. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Music Education from Arizona State University.

presenters.name: Sean Ryan
presenters.bio: Sean Ryan, M.S., is a Research Associate, and holds a Master of Science in Biochemistry from the University of Arizona. He taught nine years in the classroom as a certified K-8 educator. He works at the Center for Science Teaching and Learning at Northern Arizona University. His expertise includes STEM community education and outreach, design of professional development activities and resources, program implementation, and partnership development.

presenters.name: Shannon C. Scott, D.O., FACOFP
presenters.bio: Shannon Scott, D.O., FACOFP, is a distinguished osteopathic family physician, medical educator, and advocate serving as the Medical Director of the Midwestern University Multispecialty Clinic and Assistant Dean and Clinical Professor at the Arizona College of Osteopathic Medicine (AZCOM). A 2004 AZCOM alumna, she established her leadership early as HonorHealth’s first osteopathic physician Chief Resident before joining the University faculty in 2008. For over 18 years, Dr. Scott has served the Glendale community, seamlessly blending frontline clinical excellence with the training of tomorrow's physicians. Beyond the clinic and classroom, Dr. Scott champions her profession nationally as an American Osteopathic Association (AOA) Trustee and regionally as a Past-President of the Arizona Osteopathic Medical Association. A graduate of the AOA Health Policy Fellowship and a Fellow of the American College of Osteopathic Family Physicians, her expertise is recognized at the state level through her appointment to the Arizona State Telemedicine Committee. Recently completing her M.B.A. from the University of Arizona, Dr. Scott continues to drive systemic innovation, workforce advocacy, and patient-centered leadership across the healthcare landscape.

presenters.name: Sheila James
presenters.bio: Sheila is a transformative leader with over 25 years of experience in youth development, known for elevating the quality of programs that serve children and youth. Her expertise in coaching, training, and mentoring equips educators and program staff with innovative strategies and practical tools. With a keen eye on trends in afterschool and early childhood education, Sheila stays ahead of the curve to ensure excellence in the field. Her dedication to equity and empowering others has been the cornerstone of her impactful and purpose-driven leadership.

presenters.name: Sheryl Roehl
presenters.bio: Dr. Roehl is part of the Texas Advanced Computing Center EPIC (Expanding Pathways in Computing) WeTeach_CS team. She serves as the EPIC Partnership Coordinator. She has worked with school districts to develop and implement K-12 Computer Science Pathways. She works with WeTeach_CS to provide training in Computational Thinking, Scratch, Foundations of Computer Science for Teachers, Experience CS, Rural Opportunities in Computer Science, CS Jumpstart, Code.org Fundamentals and Discoveries, Artificial Intelligence and Launch CS. Her previous work experience includes fifteen years as a math/science/STEM specialist for Region 3 Education Service Center, six years serving as the Assistant Director of the South Texas Rural Systemic Initiative funded by NSF and twelve years as a high school math, science and programming teacher. Sheryl is a Texas Instruments T3 Regional Trainer and a Code.org CSF and CSD facilitator. She is a 2024, 2025 and 2026 micro:bit Champion and currently presents training sessions for Cyber.org.
