presenters.name: Stephanie McGrew
presenters.bio: Dr. Stephanie McGrew is the Director of the Department of Diversity & Inclusion at A.T. Still University, where she leads initiatives focused on student engagement, educational access, and career pathway development. She oversees Dreamline Pathways™, a nationwide award-winning initiative that connects K–12 and undergraduate students to health and STEM careers through hands-on learning, simulation, mentorship, internships, and immersive campus experiences. Her work centers on building meaningful partnerships between educators, communities, and higher education to help students explore career possibilities, develop confidence, and envision themselves as future STEM and healthcare professionals.

presenters.name: Stephanie Rodriguez
presenters.bio: Dr. Stephanie Rodriguez is the Director of the STEMM Opportunity Alliance at the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS), where she leads a national cross-sector coalition catalyzing access to STEMM learning and workforce. Previously, Dr. Rodriguez served as a STEM Next Senior Workforce Fellow at the U.S. Department of Labor’s Employment and Training Administration. There, she developed and launched the Youth Employment Works strategy, connecting young people to workforce opportunities tied to federal investments in infrastructure, space, semiconductors, and clean energy. Her contributions earned her a Secretary’s Honor Award. Her federal experience includes work at the National Science Foundation on computer science education and the CSforALL movement. She later served as STEM Policy Director at the Afterschool Alliance, expanding access to STEM and computer science in out-of-school programs. As VP of Policy and Engagement at AnitaB.org, she led tech workforce policy initiatives and managed relationships with Congress and the Executive Branch. She also served as Federal Partnership Director at Tech Talent Project, supporting efforts to recruit modern technical leaders into government. An immunologist by training, Dr. Rodriguez applies evidence-based approaches to education, workforce development, and equity. She earned her B.S. from Stanford University and Ph.D. in Immunology from Washington University in St. Louis.

presenters.name: Tara Henderson
presenters.bio: Tara Zollinger Henderson is the Director of Education at Explora Science Center and Children’s Museum in Albuquerque, New Mexico. She leads the development, implementation, and evaluation of inquiry-based science education programs serving schools, families, and communities across the state. Her work centers on hands-on learning, educator professional development, and building sustained community partnerships that support meaningful STEM engagement. Tara holds graduate degrees in family studies and nonprofit management, and her research interests include informal learning environments, place-based education, and the role of museums in supporting lifelong learning.

presenters.name: Wesley Schofield
presenters.bio: Wesley has been creating video content for 10+ years. Born and raised in Willcox, Arizona, he spent his life learning to create graphics, videos, and audio content. Wesley is a passionate creative with a desire to teach others. In 2018 Wesley entered the professional world of videography, producing hundreds of videos from advertisements, music videos, an award winning documentary, and tutorials spanning both the fine arts and digital arts worlds. Community and economic development has been a driving force in Wesley’s life. Belonging to his hometown’s Skatepark Committee and Downtown Revitalization Project, he cares deeply about the communities he is a part of.

presenters.name: Yir Glora Yueh, Ph.D.
presenters.bio: Gloria Yueh, Ph.D., Senior Vice President and Provost, serves as Midwestern University’s senior academic leader, overseeing academic quality across a comprehensive portfolio of health sciences and professional education programs. She brings more than two decades of progressive experience in academic leadership, faculty affairs, curriculum development, and research administration, with a strong record of advancing program growth, strengthening faculty engagement, guiding accreditation efforts, and promoting research scholarship across disciplines. Dr. Yueh earned her Ph.D. in Biochemistry from the University of Connecticut and completed postdoctoral training at Mayo Clinic–Scottsdale. She also holds a Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering from National Taiwan University. Her national professional service includes roles as COMAT FBAS Biochemistry Discipline Lead with the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners and as National Faculty in Biochemistry and Genetics for the National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners. In her current role, Dr. Yueh provides strategic leadership across all colleges at Midwestern University, with expertise in curricular innovation, intercollegiate collaboration, and research administration, all in support of student success. As a member of the executive leadership team, she brings scholarly rigor and strategic vision to advance the University’s mission and long-term growth.

presenters.name: Yvonda Shelton
presenters.bio: Yvonnda Shelton is a Workforce Development at SciTech Institute, where she works to close the gap between classroom learning and career readiness across Arizona. She supports the development and statewide rollout of the Arizona Skills Map Framework, partnering with schools, employers, and community organizations to build shared pathways between education and industry. She leads the Worlds of Work initiative, connecting students directly with local employers through hands-on career exploration events. Yvonnda serves on the Maricopa County Workforce Board Youth Committee and she brings a practical, on-the-ground perspective to the systems-level work of building a stronger STEM talent pipeline for across Arizona.

presenters.name: Zachary Beam
presenters.bio: Zachary Beam is a high school science teacher at Newcastle High School in Wyoming, where he has spent the past thirteen years creating student-centered STEM learning experiences built around curiosity, problem solving, and real-world challenges. He helped develop the school's makerspace through grant funding and community support and believes students learn best when they are given the freedom to explore ideas, make mistakes, and demonstrate understanding in meaningful ways. Outside the classroom, Zach enjoys exploring the outdoors with his wife and young son and volunteers with a local trails organization to support trail development and outdoor recreation opportunities in Weston County, Wyoming. When he's not teaching or on the trails, he's usually buried in a project that's a little outside his comfort zone, whether that's building, fixing, learning, or figuring out how to do something he has never done before.

presenters.name: Zhuoying Wang
presenters.bio: Zhuoying Wang earned her Ph.D. in Educational Psychology from Texas A&M University. She is currently a Research Associate at the Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) Evaluation Service at The University of Texas at Austin. Her research focuses on program evaluation, STEM education, language development, and quantitative research methods. Zhuoying has led the evaluation of multiple initiatives designed to strengthen student outcomes and enhance teacher capacity in STEM education and language development.
